what: W. R. Berkley is an American insurance holding company made up of more than fifty separate businesses, each underwriting a specific type of commercial risk. It is one of the largest writers of excess and surplus lines, the insurance for risks standard insurers will not take.
customers: Businesses buying commercial and specialty insurance, and insurers buying reinsurance.
money: excess and surplus lines, admitted commercial lines and specialty personal
moat: Dozens of specialist underwriting teams given authority over their own niches, which lets it price risks that larger, more centralised insurers misjudge.
risks: Commercial insurance pricing has softened after several strong years
Reserve adequacy on liability policies is an industry-wide concern
Catastrophe losses can be large in any single year
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: Revenue grew about 8% last year and about 10% a year over three years
Excess and surplus lines grow when standard insurers retreat from difficult risks
A long record of growing book value per share faster than peers
watch: The combined ratio and net premium growth in excess and surplus lines.
